mcqs.q: Autacoids are best described as:
opts: Biological factors that act like local hormones
mcqs.explain: Autacoids act like local hormones, regulating blood flow, inflammation, pain and smooth-muscle tone.

mcqs.q: Which is an autacoid?
mcqs.explain: Autacoids include histamine, serotonin, prostaglandins, leukotrienes, bradykinin and angiotensin.

mcqs.q: Histamine release classically causes:
opts: Vasodilation, increased vascular permeability and itching
mcqs.explain: Histamine produces vasodilation, increased vascular permeability and itching — features of allergy and inflammation.

mcqs.q: The H1 receptor mediates ___, blocked by ___:
mcqs.explain: H1 mediates vasodilation, bronchoconstriction and itching and is blocked by H1 antihistamines like diphenhydramine.

mcqs.q: The H2 receptor is responsible for ___ and is blocked by ___:
mcqs.explain: H2 receptors stimulate gastric acid secretion; H2 blockers (famotidine, ranitidine) reduce acid (useful before surgery).

mcqs.q: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, diclofenac) reduce pain and inflammation by inhibiting:
mcqs.explain: NSAIDs inhibit COX enzymes, decreasing prostaglandin synthesis and thereby inflammation and pain sensitization.

mcqs.q: Prostaglandins in tissue primarily act as:
opts: Inflammatory mediators that sensitize pain and regulate blood flow
mcqs.explain: Prostaglandins (eicosanoids) are inflammatory mediators that sensitize pain receptors and regulate blood flow.

mcqs.q: Misoprostol, a prostaglandin analogue, is used to:
mcqs.explain: Misoprostol is a prostaglandin used for gastric ulcer prevention (and other obstetric uses).

mcqs.q: Leukotrienes are involved in bronchoconstriction and allergy; they are blocked by:
mcqs.explain: Montelukast is a leukotriene inhibitor used in asthma and allergic conditions.

mcqs.q: Serotonin (5-HT) functions include:
opts: Vasoconstriction, platelet aggregation, mood and pain regulation, peristalsis
mcqs.explain: 5-HT contributes to vasoconstriction, platelet aggregation, mood/pain perception and peristalsis.

mcqs.q: Sumatriptan, a 5-HT agonist, is used to treat:
mcqs.explain: Sumatriptan is a serotonin (5-HT) agonist used to treat migraine; buspirone (5-HT) is used for anxiety.

mcqs.q: Ondansetron, a 5-HT antagonist, is used as a(n):
mcqs.explain: Ondansetron blocks 5-HT at the vomiting centres/chemoreceptor trigger zone; metoclopramide is also antiemetic/prokinetic.

mcqs.q: Why are SSRIs important in dental surgery?
mcqs.explain: SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) can increase bleeding risk during surgery, an important dental consideration.

mcqs.q: Bradykinin acts on B₂ receptors to cause:
mcqs.explain: Bradykinin is a potent vasodilator acting on B₂ receptors, increasing vascular permeability and stimulating pain receptors.

mcqs.q: Icatibant works by:
mcqs.explain: Icatibant competitively blocks B₂ receptors, preventing bradykinin's vasodilator/pain effects.

mcqs.q: ACE inhibitors (lisinopril, enalapril) lower blood pressure but may cause the dental side effect of:
mcqs.explain: ACE inhibitors can cause xerostomia, raising the risk of caries and oral infections.

mcqs.q: A key side effect of NSAIDs relevant to dentistry is:
opts: GI bleeding, renal impairment and prolonged bleeding time
mcqs.explain: NSAIDs can cause GI bleeding, renal impairment and a prolonged bleeding time — important before surgery.

mcqs.q: Antihistamines commonly cause which dental-relevant side effects?
mcqs.explain: H1 antihistamines (e.g. diphenhydramine) cause dry mouth and drowsiness.

mcqs.q: Which H1 antihistamine is used for allergic reactions in dentistry?
mcqs.explain: Diphenhydramine is an H1 blocker used to treat allergic reactions (e.g. to dental materials/medications).

mcqs.q: An H2 blocker may be given before surgery to:
mcqs.explain: H2 blockers (famotidine/ranitidine) reduce gastric acid secretion, sometimes given peri-operatively.

mcqs.q: ACE inhibitors increase levels of which autacoid (contributing to cough)?
mcqs.explain: ACE normally degrades bradykinin; ACE inhibitors raise bradykinin (linked to the characteristic dry cough).

mcqs.q: Which autacoid is most directly targeted by NSAIDs?
mcqs.explain: NSAIDs inhibit COX, reducing prostaglandin production — the main analgesic/anti-inflammatory mechanism.

saqs.q: Define autacoids and list four examples.
saqs.a: Biological factors acting as local hormones. Examples: histamine, serotonin, prostaglandins, leukotrienes, bradykinin, angiotensin.

saqs.q: Describe the histamine receptors H1 and H2 and their blockers.
saqs.a: H1: vasodilation, bronchoconstriction, itching → blocked by diphenhydramine. H2: gastric acid secretion → blocked by famotidine/ranitidine.

saqs.q: How do NSAIDs work and what is their dental side-effect profile?
saqs.a: NSAIDs inhibit COX, reducing prostaglandins (pain/inflammation). Side effects: GI bleeding, renal impairment, prolonged bleeding time.

saqs.q: Give a 5-HT agonist and antagonist with their uses.
What is the role of bradykinin and how is it blocked?
saqs.a: Bradykinin acts on B₂ receptors → vasodilation, ↑ permeability and pain. Icatibant competitively blocks B₂.

saqs.q: Why are ACE inhibitors relevant in dentistry?
saqs.a: They lower BP but cause dry mouth (xerostomia), increasing caries and oral-infection risk; they also raise bradykinin.

saqs.q: Match each drug to its autacoid and condition: montelukast, sumatriptan, antihistamine.
saqs.a: Montelukast → leukotrienes → asthma; sumatriptan → serotonin → migraine; antihistamine → histamine → allergy.
